Subject: Senior Inference Engineer — scope, interviewer checklist & scoring

Hi all,

We start interviews for the Senior Inference Engineer (REQ-1245) next week. Before we kick off, I want a short calibration so everyone is aligned on scope, what separates a solid senior from a stretch candidate, and the exact evidence we want from each interviewer.

Attached: Senior_Inference_Rubric_v0.3.pdf and the provisional schedule (Interview_Schedule.ics). Key asks:
- Review the rubric and call out any missing focus areas by EOD Wed.
- Marissa: as bar-raiser, can you confirm the anchoring language we want for pass vs. strong-pass?
- Vivek/Aditya: confirm who will take system design, coding pair, and debugging probes.
- Everyone: commit to one concrete evidence bullet and an anchor rating (1-5) after each interview.

A couple of context notes on the role:
- This is primarily a production serving role — emphasis on inference runtime performance, KV cache behavior, and root-cause debugging of tail latency incidents.
- We need someone who can influence product tradeoffs (cost vs latency) with concrete measurements and plan rollouts for model variants.

If we agree, I propose a 20-minute calibration call Thu 9:30am PT — quick run through rubric and one mock anchor.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> We start interviews for the Senior Inference Engineer (REQ-1245) next week...

Thanks, Irene — this looks good. A few quick suggested edits to the rubric and interviewer commitments:

1) Focus areas (add / emphasize):
   - Runtime performance troubleshooting (profiling GPU kernels, memory/host transfer hotspots)
   - Prefix/KV cache correctness and cache invalidation strategies
   - Quantization and precision tradeoffs for 8-bit/4-bit in production
   - Observability: tracing token latency back through batched pipelines

2) Scoring weights (proposal):
   - System design & architecture: 30%
   - Debugging / incident RCA: 25%
   - Coding / implementation (pair): 20%
   - Mentorship and communication: 15%
   - Culture / team fit: 10%

3) Evidence asks for interviewers (short):
   - One-sentence anchor rating (1-5)
   - Two bullets: specific behavior/answer + reproduction or test they'd ask for

4) Quick probes to add to the kit:
   - "Describe a time you traced a tail-latency issue to a batching edge case."
   - "How would you measure the cost impact of KV cache misses across traffic?"

I'm happy to take the system design slot and lead the debugging probes. Thu 9:30am PT works for a quick align.

-Vivek

Thanks for kicking this off, Irene. A few bar-raiser notes and concrete language we should add to the rubric: 

Bar-raiser principles to include:
- Depth over breadth: for Senior, prefer demonstrated deep ownership (led a rollout, owned metrics) rather than superficial familiarity with many subsystems.
- Evidence-first: every rating must point to a candidate action/outcome (logs they would check, an optimization they executed).
- Growth signal: preference for folks who show a trajectory to Principal (mentoring, technical influence).

Suggested pass/strong-pass anchors (short):
- Pass (3): Candidate shows independent ownership of an inference service, can identify the main sources of latency and propose reasonable mitigations with trade-offs.
- Strong-pass (4): Candidate led a measurable latency/cost improvement project; can point to data and tradeoffs, and articulated clear rollout/rollback criteria.
- Blocker (1-2): Can't reason about basic batching/cache interactions or cannot propose measurable mitigations.

Interviewer deliverable (enforce):
- After each interview: 1-line anchor rating + 2 supporting bullets (one technical detail, one behavioral/impact example).

Probe bank (to pick from):
- "Walk me through a time you diagnosed an intermittent production regression tied to model serving."
- "If an older model variant suddenly has higher latency in region X, what telemetry would you check first and why?"
- "Show me on a whiteboard: how KV cache keys are generated and what a stale key scenario looks like."

I can run the 20-minute calibration Thu 9:30am PT and play the mock anchor (I will role-play a marginal candidate). Also: please include this short bar-raiser checklist in the rubric PDF as an appendix (Irene, if you want I can edit the doc).

Marissa
